newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: U.S.'s Davidow seeks transparent Argentine tenders.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s Davidow seeks transparent Argentine tenders.

text.p: U.S. Assistant Secretary for Inter-American Affairs Jeffrey Davidow was quoted Tuesday as saying Argentina's privatizations must be totally transparent.
"What matters in Argentina, as in the United States, is transparency," he told Clarin newspaper.
"In any country there are always suspicions. Then, the only way to face those suspicions is to have totally transparent (privatization) processes."

Davidow was answering a question whether the U.S. government was expecting greater transparency in state selloffs after U.S. companies for the most part lost out in the first stage of Argentine privatizations launched in 1989.
Asked whether Argentina's lack of ratification of the Organization of American States anticorruption convention was a flaw in Argentina's fight against corruption, Davidow said:
"That convention was very important but even more important are the national laws against corruption. Then, the most important thing is to have open, clean, transparent (tender) processes."
